newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says no change in local dollar policy.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says no change in local dollar policy.

text.p: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said on Friday there was no fundamental shift in its policy of not internationalising the Singapore dollar.

Responding to queries on whether there were plans to liberalise further the Singapore dollar after foreign firms were allowed to convert or list their shares in Singapore dollars, MAS deputy managing director Koh Beng Seng said:
"There is no fundamental change but there is a technical change. There is no fundamental change in (the) policy of not internationalising the Singapore dollar."
Koh was speaking at a news conference on Singapore's third quarter economic survey.

Finance Minister Richard Hu said in October measures to allow some foreign firms to list and trade their shares in Singapore dollars were in line with the MAS's policy of allowing the gradual internationalisation of its currency.
Hu said in 1995 that Singapore's tough policy of not letting its currency be traded internationally would be gradually relaxed but still within tight limits.
At that time Hu described the relaxation of policy as a "rearguard action", reflecting the reality of the market place.
